findings.claim: A valid backup code plus any non-empty dummy totpCode logs the user in without the password. The pre-existing password gate (~line 119-121) only runs when !credentials.totpCode. The new backup-code branch at 131 is taken whenever backupCode is set and never checks totpCode. One static, exfiltratable code is therefore enough to authenticate.
findings.evidence: Reasoned only, not executed by either seat. open-code-review: POST /api/auth/callback/credentials with email, password='', totpCode=x and a valid backupCode should return a session. superpowers: the csrf plus callback curl sequence with password=wrong&totpCode=000000&backupCode=<valid> should set a session cookie. Before the patch, a non-empty totpCode still had to pass totpAuthenticatorCheck.
findings.reason: Raised by 2 seats (fewer than 3), so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed under the merge rule. Severity is normalised to Critical (superpowers: Critical, open-code-review: Important). Not rejected, because no report disproves it. Unverified. Flagged for the user: this is the most severe finding in the review, and both correctness seats raised it independently, but the agreement threshold still keeps it off the main list.

findings.claim: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read, decrypt, null-slot, write-back with no transaction or compare-and-swap. Concurrent logins with the same code all succeed. Last-write-wins can also restore a code that another concurrent login just consumed.
findings.evidence: Reasoned only. open-code-review cites lines 140-156 and suggests updateMany where {id, backupCodes: old} with count === 1. superpowers M1 cites lines 136-156. ponytail notes the check-then-write race outside its brief. The rate limit narrows the window but does not close it.
findings.reason: 3 seats, so main list. Severity is normalised to Important (open-code-review: Important, superpowers: Minor). ponytail's vote is an unscored out-of-brief note. Before any fix it needs a red test: parallel authorize() calls with the same code must not both succeed. Unverified until that test exists.

verifier.reason: At packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139-156 the code reads user.backupCodes, decrypts it, finds the code with indexOf, sets that slot to null and writes the array back with a plain prisma.user.update keyed only on id. There is no transaction and no check that the stored value is unchanged, so concurrent logins with the same code all pass, and two concurrent logins with different codes can each overwrite the other's nulled slot.

findings.claim: After enabling, onEnable() (and so utils.viewer.me.invalidate()) runs only from the backup-codes Close button. Dismissing with Esc, an overlay click or the X goes through onOpenChange, which only toggles open. The settings switch and badge then show 2FA disabled while it is enabled in the DB. resetState never runs, so reopening shows the stale DisplayBackupCodes step.
findings.evidence: Reasoned only. superpowers proposes a red Playwright test: in 'should allow a user to disable 2FA', replace the backup-codes-close click with page.keyboard.press('Escape'). The existing data-state='checked' expectation should then fail. Parent: apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:62-72.
findings.reason: 3 seats, so main list. Severity is normalised to Important (superpowers: Important, open-code-review: Minor). ponytail's vote is an unscored out-of-brief note about resetState. superpowers' Escape variant is the red test to run before fixing. Unverified until it fails on the pinned code.

verifier.reason: After a successful enable, EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 only sets the DisplayBackupCodes step. resetState() and onEnable() run only from the backup-codes-close button (lines 266-269), while Esc or an overlay click goes through onOpenChange, which at two-factor-auth.tsx:64 just toggles enableModalOpen. So viewer.me is never invalidated, the switch and badge stay stale, and because the modal stays mounted, reopening shows the old backup-codes step.

findings.claim: None of the new backup-code auth paths has a test: login with a backup code, rejection of a used code, a wrong code, the missing-codes case, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The only new e2e steps click Download, Copy and Close. The patch leaves TODOs admitting the gap.
findings.evidence: The patch's own comments: '// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup', '// TODO: check file content' and '// TODO: check clipboard content' (lines 110-125). This breaches the PR template's 'added tests that prove ... my feature works' and the CONTRIBUTING e2e guidance. open-code-review notes the gap is why its findings 1 and 2 would pass CI.
findings.reason: 4 seats, so main list. Severity is normalised to Important (superpowers I3: Important, the others: Minor). open-code-review's vote is from its 'Not checked' section. The fix is the tests themselves: backup-code login succeeds once and is then rejected on reuse, and disable works with a backup code. These guard the main-list race finding and the appendix password-bypass finding.

verifier.reason: The only test file the patch touches is apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts. Its new steps just click backup-codes-download (checking only the filename), backup-codes-copy and backup-codes-close, and it leaves TODOs for 'login + disabling 2fa with backup', file content and clipboard content. No test covers the new backup-code paths in next-auth-options.ts or totp/disable.ts: login, a used code, a wrong code, missing codes, or disabling 2FA.

findings.claim: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...) runs on an unvalidated body. A truthy non-string backupCode (number, array, object) throws a TypeError and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.
findings.evidence: Reasoned only, not executed. The fix is a typeof === 'string' check before use.
findings.reason: 3 seats, so main list. mattpocock's vote is an unscored out-of-brief note. Minor and accepted. A red request test (POST with backupCode: 123, expect 400) is cheap and should come first.

verifier.reason: At apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48 the only check on req.body.backupCode is that it is truthy, and line 61 then calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""). A JSON number, array or object has no replaceAll method, so the call throws a TypeError that nothing catches and the request returns a 500 instead of a 400. This happens only after the password check passes and only if the user has stored backup codes.

findings.claim: The comparison is an exact, case-sensitive indexOf after stripping only '-', with no toLowerCase or trim. Codes are lowercase hex, the placeholder is XXXXX-XXXXX, and the input lacks autoCapitalize='off'. Uppercase, auto-capitalized or whitespace-padded codes are rejected as IncorrectBackupCode. This hits users who have lost their authenticator. The same issue exists at disable.ts:61 and BackupCode.tsx:17-26.
findings.evidence: Executed by superpowers: node -e with indexOf('Abcde-12345'.replaceAll('-','')) on ['abcde12345'] prints -1. The iOS auto-capitalization impact (~37.5% of codes) is reasoned.
findings.reason: 2 seats, so appendix and not fixed under the merge rule. Severity is normalised to Important (superpowers: Important, open-code-review: Minor). The case mismatch has an executed repro. The real-world impact is reasoned.

findings.claim: Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have backupCodes = null. They get 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.', but no regenerate path exists while 2FA is on. Getting codes needs disable/re-enable, which needs the authenticator they have lost.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. Paths are next-auth-options.ts:136 and disable.ts:54, and no regeneration endpoint or UI exists.

findings.claim: When the encryption key is missing, the new backup-code branch does throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) instead of res.status(500).json(...). The rest of the file uses the latter, so this is an unhandled 500.

coverage: Files skipped: none. All four seats report reading all 16 patch files. mattpocock, ponytail and superpowers gave only a quick look to the trivial migration SQL, schema.prisma, builder.ts, ErrorCode.ts and locale lines. superpowers also flagged one file outside the patch (inviteMemberUtils.test.ts). Axes that did not run: (1) The gate was not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored: no build, lint, prettier, type-check, unit or e2e results exist, and seats could not run them (no node_modules). (2) Spec axis: no spec, and no commit references an issue. (3) Standards axis ran against CONTRIBUTING.md, the PR template and the eslint/prettier presets only. The repo has no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or coding-standards doc. (4) No reviewer from another model family was used. Evidence quality: nearly every claim is reasoned. The only executed check is superpowers' node -e case-sensitivity repro. The password-bypass, race, dialog-state and type-error findings have not been run against code. Merge choices: out-of-brief or 'not checked' notes were counted as seat votes, and the reason field says so where it decided main-list placement (race, dialog state, replaceAll 500, test gap).
